text: The first tracks of the Battalion reached the beach at about 1030 hours, and by 1400 hours all personnel and vehicles of the Battalion were ashore and the AAA weapons were in positions in defense of the Division beaches.
note: D-Day of the southern France landing (Operation Dragoon), near Sainte-Maxime. No enemy aircraft attacked the beaches that day.

text: Two ME 109's flying at cruising speed in the vicinity of J-546416 was fired on by guns of Battery "D". One of the planes was definitely destroyed.
note: Four detachments of Battery D were defending Battery A of the 976th FA at J-546416, near Moirans (Lambert Zone III grid). The narrative counts it as the one plane destroyed in August.

text: Two ME 109's strafing from an altitude of 200 feet were engaged by Battery "D" and one of these was probably destroyed as many hits were observed. Thirteen rounds of 37mm and 1,050 rounds of 50 cal...
note: Battery D's CP that day was J-552408, near Moirans.

text: This Battalion engaged two ME 109's on reconnaissance flying at an approximate altitude of 50 to 75 feet. Batteries "A" and "D" expended a total of 17 rounds of 37mm and 1,100 rounds of cal. 50...
Two ME 109's ... strafed elements of the 189th Field Artillery which is defended by Battery "D" ... Numerous 50 cal. hits were observed entering the plane head-on.
note: Near Baume-les-Dames (Doubs). 27 rounds of 37mm and 850 of .50 cal.

text: Two ME 109's flying at an approximate altitude of 100 feet with top cover of two FW 190's. Battery "D" expended 200 rounds ... out of range of "D" Battery's guns, but seventh detachment of "D" Battery fired to warn adjacent units...

About fifty (50) Germans escaping from the south on foot, passed near the third detachment of "D" Battery in the vicinity of P-143850. The sentry on duty endeavored to halt them and fired upon them when they ran. All but six ... were captured shortly thereafter by elements of the 179th Infantry.
note: Placed at the detachment's position (Lambert Zone II grid), 4.6 km east of Abbenans, where the battery's station was. The month's narrative credits the capture to "alertness of a sentry on duty at a gun section of Battery D" (p09).

text: Batteries "C" and "D" engaged two ME 109's which flew at an approximate altitude of from 100 to 600 feet ... Mission of the enemy aircraft was strafing. Hits reported by both Batteries.

Two ME 109's ... strafed ... Batteries "C" and "D" expended a total of 121 rounds of 37mm and 3,375 rounds of cal. 50... One plane was observed to have burst into flames when engaged by 37mm. A 179th Infantry patrol reported plane crashed in vicinity of CHENIMENIL and pilot was dead.
note: Placed at the crash, which four eyewitness certificates confirmed.

text: Batteries "C" and "D" engaged one ME 109 ... at an approximate altitude of from 75 to 600 feet ... No damage reported on enemy aircraft.
This Battalion engaged 2 ME 109's on reconnaissance ... Batteries B and D expended a total of 142 rounds of 37mm and 6,440 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition in barrage fire without result.
note: Near Rambervillers.

text: One ME 109 ... straffed in the vicinity of Q-845275. Plane took violent evasive action when engaged. Batteries "B" and "D" expended a total of 91 rounds of 37mm and 2,250 rounds of cal. 50, "B" Battery shooting off the tail... Enemy pilot was seen to bail out over forward lines.
note: Placed where the plane strafed (Obermodern). The tail is credited to Battery B.

text: One ME 109 ... on armed reconnaissance was engaged by this Battalion without result. Batteries "B", "C", and "D" expended a total of 196 rounds of 37mm and 7,000 rounds...
This Battalion engaged four ME 109's which straffed in the vicinity of Zutzendorf ... Batteries "B" and "D" expended a total of 8 rounds of 37mm and 400 rounds of cal. 50 ... without result.

Eight P-47's ... bearing American markings ... committed hostile act by strafing... Batteries "A" and "D" engaged these aircraft. Battery "D" had one (1) 37mm hit and several cal. 50 hits on three other planes.
note: The month's narrative (p08): the P-47s of 30 and 31 December "were discovered to have been flown by German pilots".

text: Two FW 190's flying on armed reconnaissance at approximate altitude of from 1,500 to 200 feet... "D" Battery ... reported several 37mm and numerous cal. 50 hits on both planes. Pending further confirmation we claim two (2) enemy aircraft probably destroyed.

This battalion engaged one ME 109 Flying on armed reconnaissance at an altitude of from 100 to 200 feet. Battery "D" expended 30 rounds of 37mm and 1,537 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition. Plane strafed in the vicinity of R-007378.
note: Placed where the plane strafed (near Wœrth).

text: Two P-47's approached ... one of which flew too low and crashed ... The remaining P-47 having a red tail, circled ... and strafed... Battery D expended 35 rounds of 37mm and 1,650 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition at this aircraft in the vicinity of ZUTZENDORF.
note: "Both planes were identified by Air Support Officer of 45th Infantry Division to have been friendly" (p05).

text: One P-51 bearing American markings ... Plane continued to Q-7831 grid and strafed Batteries "A" and "B" of 693rd F.A. Battalion at which time 2nd Platoon of "D" Battery, this organization engaged.
note: It crashed near Q-834264, killing the pilot. Whose it was isn't said.

text: 2 Me 109's on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector ... were engaged by all Batteries. Numerous 37mm and .50 Cal. hits were observed by B, C, and D Batteries on both planes. Pilot of one Me 109 bailed out... Plane crashed vic. Q-805330.
note: Placed at the crash (Ingwiller). Claimed one definite and one probable; February's only engagement.

text: Between 0030 and 0130 Batteries A, C, and D, engaged enemy A/C flying from 400 to 4500 feet. Plane believed to have crashed in the vicinity of M-4820. No claims.
note: The night of the 45th Division's Rhine crossing near Worms. Placed at the 1 km square where the plane was believed down.

text: Batteries B, C, and D engaged two (2) ME-109's on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector... without results.

Two (2) ME-109's were engaged by all units of this battalion. Enemy aircraft strafed positions of the 189th Field Artillery Bn area and the highway in the vicinity of M-977495 without damage. Battery D observed hits and the pilot was seen to bail out... Plane was later confirmed as definitely destroyed.
One ME 262, flying at 3500 to 6000 feet on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector, was engaged by batteries A, C, and D... without result.
note: Battery D also engaged the jets with all batteries at 0655, 0713 and 1445, and with Battery B at 1133; none hit.

text: Two (2) missions of one (1) ME-262 each, on armed reconnaissance flying at 1500 to 2500 feet were engaged by all batteries. Results were several .50 cal. hits observed.
A Pfc of Battery D was wounded by enemy shell fragment during a barrage.
note: The record names him.

text: One (1) M-16, 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired 100 rounds of .50 cal ammunition at enemy foot troops at coordinates H-825085, wounding one (1) and capturing three (3) prisoners of war.
note: Typed square H, as in the journal's Ostheim (H-775093). Falls at Eußenhausen, near Mellrichstadt.

text: The 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired four (4) ground missions at enemy foot troops in the vicinity O-2257. Results were a machine gun neutralized; fires observed; and enemy dispersed.
note: Near Godeldorf (Baunach), which Battery C helped clear next day. 88 rounds of 37mm and 750 of .50 cal.

text: Three men of Battery D were wounded by an 88mm shell that hit their M-15 half-track. One, a corporal, later died of his wounds.
note: The record names all three. Placed with the 2nd Platoon's missions that day; the shell's position isn't given.

text: There were three (3) missions of FW-190s, total of twenty-nine (29) enemy planes ... engaged by all batteries. Several hits were observed and one (1) FW-190 was seen to go down smoking in the vicinity of O-233568.
note: Placed where the plane went down (Kemmern). Claimed one probable.

text: Four missions by a total of six (6) ME-262s, one (1) ME-109, and six (6) FW-190s on armed reconnaissance and bombing missions ... Planes were engaged by Batteries B, C, and D. Several 37mm and .50 cal. hits were observed.
A corporal of Battery D suffered concussion as a result of friendly gun fire.
note: The record names him.

text: There were four (4) missions by a total of eighteen (18) enemy aircraft ... engaged by Batteries B, C, and D. Results were several 37mm and .50 cal hits observed by Battery B.
Three (3) missions by a total of four (4) JU-87s and four (4) ME-262s ... were engaged by all batteries. No hits were reported.
Six (6) ME-262s flying at 500 to 5000 feet attacking B-26 Bombers were engaged by Batteries C and D without result.
note: At 1725 another Me 262 was engaged by Batteries C and D, also without result.

text: One (1) M-16, 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired at enemy personnel at coordinates T-684045. Results are unknown. Ammunition expenditures: 400 rounds .50 cal.
note: Near Waidhofen (Schrobenhausen).

text: Fired on Enemy target at 2100 Weather Good
note: Battery C's own morning report, 2 mi E of Oran. Its only firing at Oran. The report says "target", not aircraft: for an anti-aircraft gun battery that means aircraft (inferred). No time zone typed. No Oran paper of these days is on Gallica. L'Écho d'Alger of 21 and 22 Jan 1943 (gallica:bpt6k7586936d, gallica:bpt6k7586937t) has no raid on Oran; on 22 Jan it reports alerts at Algiers "dans la soirée du 20 au 21 Janvier": the raiders met "un violent barrage de D.C.A.", a few bombs, little damage. That was Algiers, about 400 km east; Oran was raided that night, by the Italian side's account: the Italian Supreme Command's Bulletin no. 971, issued the afternoon of 21 Jan (La Stampa, 22 Jan, lastampa:1943-01-22/p1): "Velivoli italiani a grande raggio di azione hanno agito sul porto di Orano; una nave è stata lasciata in fiamme ed un'altra gravemente danneggiata." The paper's account of the same night ("L'incursione su Orano", same page): long-range bombers that had left "una base avanzata" in the afternoon reached Oran after a long flight over the sea and, against "la violentissima reazione delle difese nemiche", bombed the crowded port; it names two crew captains, tenenti piloti Giano Rossi and Antonio D'Alò. The unit is not named. These are the attackers' claims; the battery's fire at 2100 is on the same night, which is a match by date only. The unit, from a secondary account: the 274ª Squadriglia Bombardamento a Grande Raggio's two Piaggio P.108B four-engined bombers, from Sardinia: "Il 20 gennaio i velivoli dei ten. D'Alò e Rossi chiudono questo ciclo operativo con un'impegnativa missione sul porto di Orano"; Rossi's aircraft met an enemy night fighter, which broke off (alieuomini:piaggio_p_b,71, from Garello 1973). No loss that night is recorded there. The airfield is not named (Decimomannu likely, inferred). No. 153 Squadron RAF's Beaufighters were at Maison Blanche (Algiers) that night, not Oran: P/O Benn and Sgt Lunan destroyed a Ju 88 "about 7 miles north of Algiers" (tna:AIR 27/1027/30/p11). So the night fighter that met the P.108 over Oran was another unit's (not identified).

text: Fired on hostile targets 2050 to 2125 Weather good
note: 4 mi W of Algiers. The city's paper reports the raid: L'Écho d'Alger, 13 May 1943 (gallica:bpt6k75870445), "Alerte à Alger": an alert in the evening, enemy aircraft over the city, "La réaction de la D.C.A. a été très violente et efficace. Quelques bombes ont été lancées." Allied communiqué no. 188 of 13 May (L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May, gallica:bpt6k7587045k): bombers that tried to attack Algiers "la nuit dernière" were driven off by the anti-aircraft guns and night fighters, "Trois appareils au moins ont été détruits", a few civilian casualties, light damage. That claim is the whole defense's, not this battery's. Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed in La Stampa of 14 and 15 May mention Algiers. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 12 May 1943 (skl:45/p152): "Thirty bombers raided Algiers during the night of 12 May, scoring hits on the harbor." No losses given. The RAF night fighters' record: No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter V.8632, F/Sgt G.L. Linklater and Sgt L.V. Anthony, patrol 1935-2140, "1 JU.88 destroyed" (tna:AIR 27/1027/38/p2). The summary (tna:AIR 27/1027/37/p3): on patrol in Algiers Bay, warned of bandits 40 miles north at 16,000 ft; "The enemy aircraft which was taking evasive action from A.A. turned South about two miles West of Algiers. Our aircraft closed in and gave a two second burst. This was enough and the bandit blew up and fell into the sea. 1 Ju88 destroyed." The battery's position (4 mi W of Algiers) and fire (2050-2125) fall within that place and sortie; which guns' fire the Ju 88 was evading is not recorded (Algiers had many batteries). One aircraft of the night's raiders, by the squadron's claim.

text: Fired on hostile targets 0820 to 0822
note: 4 mi W of Algiers. Two minutes; nothing in L'Écho d'Alger of 14 May.

text: Fired on hostile targets 2136 to 2228 Weather good
note: 4 mi W of Algiers. L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943 (gallica:bpt6k7587045k), "Nouvelle alerte à Alger": an alert "hier dans la soirée", "un violent tir de barrage de la D.C.A." met the aircraft trying to fly over the city; no damage, no casualties. Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed in La Stampa of 14 and 15 May mention Algiers. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 13 May 1943 (skl:45/p163): "Algiers was attacked by 70 Ju 88s. Hits on six steamers were observed." Most likely this night (13/14 May), though it could restate the 12/13 May raid (inferred). No losses given. No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter EL.162, F/Lt S.S. Duff and Sgt R. Perfect, patrol 1930-2230, "1 JU.88 probably destroyed": "although the e/a was badly 'mauled' and lost height, he did not see it fall into the sea" (tna:AIR 27/1027/38/p3; tna:AIR 27/1027/37/p3).

text: Fired on enemy targets 2225 to 2235 Weather good Morale excellent
note: 4 mi W of Algiers. 4 Jun 1943 was a Friday. L'Écho d'Alger, 5 Jun (gallica:bpt6k7587065b), "Alerte à Alger": an alert in the evening, "On signale des dégâts et quelques victimes"; Admiral Muselier and the inspector general of civil defence (défense passive) visited the damage. 6 Jun (gallica:bpt6k7587066r), "Après l'alerte de vendredi soir": Generals Giraud and Catroux visited the bombed quarters, Catroux calling on Muslim families who had lost their homes; the Allied GHQ communiqué: "Dans la nuit du vendredi à samedi, quelques appareils ennemis ont lâché des bombes dans la région d'Alger. Il y a eu quelques victimes ... Deux bombardiers ennemis ont été détruits." The two destroyed are the whole defense's claim, not this battery's. The Axis side: Bulletin no. 1106, issued 5 Jun (La Stampa, 6 Jun, lastampa:1943-06-06/p1): "L'aviazione dell'Asse ha bombardato questa notte il porto di Algeri." The German High Command's communiqué of 5 Jun (same page): "Le installazioni portuali di Algeri sono state bombardate la scorsa notte." The attacking unit is not named. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 4 Jun 1943 (skl:46/p38): "In the evening of 4 June 19 bombers attacked Algiers. The target was covered by a smoke screen. Two planes are missing." Two of the 19 crews did not return; no record here says what brought them down. No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter V.8694, W/O R.J. Smith and Sgt J.J. Sanderson, scramble from Maison Blanche 2205-2325, "JU.88 destroyed" (tna:AIR 27/1027/40/p1), "15 miles North of Algiers" (tna:AIR 27/1027/39/p1). That is one of the two German crews missing that night, if the claim is right; the other is not accounted for in these records.

text: (AA) guns fired at enemy planes in air raid 2030
note: Battery G's own morning report, Mers-el-Kébir (the day's heading typed "Mers-El-Kebir Oran Africia"). Battery B fired at Oran the same night at 2057 (rg64-427181738/p0526). No aircraft type or result given.

text: Alert 8:57 PM fired 20 rounds at enemy planes no hits known
note: Battery B's own morning report, at the City Power Plant, Oran (as read). Battery G fired at Mers-el-Kébir the same night at 2030 (rg64-427183820/p0487).

text: Alerted 8:20 PM Port of Oran attacked by 2 enemy bombers; fired 35 rds 90MM + 34 rds .50 cal
note: Battery B's own morning report, Companie Le Bon, Oran (as read). The same night as Battery C's fire at 2100 (see its row) and Battery G's at Mers-el-Kébir, 2030-2130.

text: guns fired at enemy plane in air raid 2030 to 2130
note: Battery G's own morning report, Mers-el-Kébir, Roseville (as read). The Oran raid of 20 Jan 1943 (see Battery C's row of that date); Battery B fired at 2020.

text: Battery alerted 1855 went into action w/ 90mm Guns, No 1 Gun was out of action. 189 Rounds were fired at enemy aircraft. All clear sounded 1945. No casualties. Several known enemy air craft destroyed.
note: Battery A's own morning report, Algiers. The time is the alert: when firing began isn't given. "Several known enemy air craft destroyed" is not said to be the battery's; the city's defenses claimed three that night (see Battery C's row of this date).

text: Alerted 0805 fired 2 rds at "Ju 88 Recon Plane"
note: Battery A's own morning report, Algiers. Battery C fired 0820-0822 the same morning (its row).

text: alerted again 2145 fired 453 rds 90mm, "No 4 Gun was out of action" ... "Unofficial report of 30 enemy planes on raid of Algiers" ... all clear 2250
note: Battery A's own morning report, Algiers. The time is the alert. Battery C fired 2136-2228 (its row).

text: Battery alerted 2005 went in action against enemy aircraft 2023; fired 100 rds 90mm and 12 rds .50 cal; all clear 2050; two enemy planes reported destroyed
note: Battery A's own morning report, Algiers (as read). "Two enemy planes reported destroyed" matches the Allied communiqué's two for the whole defense (see Battery C's row of this date), not this battery's claim. Battery C's report gives 2225-2235 for its fire that night.

text: alerted 0400, Battery brought down one JU 88; 3 others by AA defense
note: Battery B's own morning report (as read); no place named in July, so placed at its last named station, Ferryville (20 Jun). The battery's own claim, unconfirmed here.

text: Provisional Platoon of 4 Guns at Maison Carrie opened fire on enemy aircraft
note: Battery H's own morning report, Algiers. No time or result given. The 4-gun platoon at Maison Carrée (now El Harrach).

text: All Guns opened fire on enemy aircraft in area of Algers and also Maison Carrie. Credited with one enemy plane
note: Battery H's own morning report, Algiers. "Credited with one enemy plane": the battery's own claim; no time given.

text: Guns at Alger opened fire on enemy aircraft at 1930 hours. Guns at Maison Carrie opened fire on enemy aircraft at 1935 hours
note: Battery H's own morning report, Algiers. No result given.

text: Action continues from previous evening till 0200 hours this date. 7 Guns opened fire on targets, but aircraft out of Range. Men on alert from previous evening
note: Battery H's own morning report, Algiers. The hour as read. The raid of the night of 20-21 Jan, continued.

text: Guns #7, 8 engaged enemy dive-bombers at 0500 ... [no] apparent damage to enemy aircraft
note: Battery H's own morning report, Algiers. The hour as read (faint); the line is cut where the two halves of the panel meet.

text: Btry alerted 0400 hours. Area flared & attacked by hostile planes 0400-0500 hours. Fired 115 rounds. 1 casualty from superficial wound.
note: Battery D's own morning report (record of events on the back of the 1 Aug form, p0085-p0086), read on the scan. The first Axis raid on Palermo after its capture: an AP dispatch "Palermo, Sicily, Aug. 1 (Delayed)" has the first planes "a little after 4 a.m., dropping flares and incendiaries ... diving to release their bombs at a low altitude" and four raiders shot down by Allied planes (Evening Star, Washington, 4 Aug 1943, p. 26, "Palermo Bombed 52 Times By Allies, Now Hit by Axis", https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn83045462/1943-08-04/ed-1/?sp=26; read on the page image). The attacking units are not identified. The casualty is not named here.

text: Area Flared and attacked by hostile planes 0355. Btry alerted 0400 hours. All clear 0512 hours. Results of firing unknown, no planes claimed. No casualties.
note: Battery D's own morning report (record of events on the back of the 4 Aug form, p0091-p0092), read on the scan. The German side: the Naval Staff's war diary, 4 Aug 1943: "On the night of 3 August, 125 of our bombers were sent out against the harbor of Palermo", claiming a destroyer and two steamers sunk and a cruiser and eight steamers damaged (skl:48/p58; the attackers' claim, not a fact). The Italian bulletin no. 1167 (lastampa:1943-08-06/p1, read on the scan) gives no night but the same figures (a destroyer and two steamers of 13,000 tons sunk, a cruiser and eight merchant ships damaged), so it reports the same raid: one claim told twice, not corroboration.

text: Battery went into action against enemy planes who dropped flares and attacked Palermo harbor from 0411 to 0650. One man slightly wounded by shrapnel. No planes claimed. Morale excellent.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 1 Aug form, p0044-p0045), read on the scan. The same raid as Battery D's 0400-0500 (p0086) and the AP dispatch of 1 Aug (Evening Star, Washington, 4 Aug 1943, p. 26). The German Naval Staff's diary records no Palermo raid that night. The wounded man is not named on this page.

text: Enemy planes dropped flares and attacked Palermo airfield and harbor, 0410. One enemy aircraft shot down. Four aircraft were seen to crash. All clear 0530. No casualties.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 4 Aug form, p0048-p0049), read on the scan. It does not say the battery fired or who shot the aircraft down: the defense's result, not the battery's. The same raid as Battery D's at 0355 (p0092): the one the German Naval Staff's diary gives as 125 bombers sent against Palermo on the night of 3 Aug (skl:48/p58).

text: Battery alerted 0430. Palermo flared and attacked. All clear 0530. No planes destroyed. No casualties.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 6 Aug form, p0051-p0052), read on the scan; the 7 Aug report is missing (the Adjutant General's target, p0053). It does not say the battery fired. Battery D has the same raid at 0425 (p0095). The other side: the Naval Staff's diary for 6 Aug, 'German Air Forces and an Italian cruiser formation carried out combined operations on the night of 5 Aug', the cruisers Eugenio di Savoia and Montecuccoli 'en route to bombard Palermo at 0431' turning back when sighted (skl:48/p85-p86); Italian bulletin no. 1168, issued 6 Aug: Italian and German bombers 'again' attacked Palermo and Augusta (lastampa:1943-08-07/p1). A match by date and hour, not an identification.

text: Area flared by hostile planes 0425. All clear at 0512. No casualties.
note: Battery D's own morning report (record of events after the 6 Aug form, p0094-p0095), read on the scan; the 7 Aug report is missing (p0096). The page also records a Purple Heart awarded on 2 Aug for a shrapnel wound in action on 1 Aug (the man is named there, not here). The same raid as Battery C's at 0430 (p0052); the other side as in that row.

text: Battery alerted 0405. Enemy planes flared and attacked Palermo harbor. One plane shot down. All clear 0500. No casualties. Morale excellent.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 23 Aug form, p0072-p0073), read on the scan. It does not say the battery fired or who shot the plane down. The German side: the Naval Staff's diary for 23 Aug, 'On the night of 22 August, 95 of our bombers attacked Palermo where hits were scored on 11 vessels totaling 55,000 GRT and on 2 destroyers and 1 probable cruiser' (skl:48/p305); Italian bulletin no. 1186, issued 24 Aug, claims eleven merchant ships and three warships hit at Palermo without a night (lastampa:1943-08-25/p1): the same claim told twice, not corroboration. The attackers' claims, not facts; the wing is not named.

text: Btry alerted 0415. Enemy planes flared & attacked Palermo Harbor. All clear 0505. No casualties. Morale excellent.
note: Battery D's own morning report (record of events after the 23 Aug form, p0116-p0117), read on the scan. The same raid as Battery C's at 0405 (p0073); the other side as in that row.

text: Battery alerted 2055, all clear 2135. No enemy action.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 9 Nov form, p0790), read on the scan. Its only alert from September to December 1943: every other day's record of events reads 'Usual field duties.' (Sep: rg64-451686722/p0847-p0879; Oct: rg64-454456048/p0571-p0632; Nov: rg64-456824820/p0772-p0834; Dec: rg64-459809807/p0660-p0690, whose forms have no record of events). The German Naval Staff's diary has no air activity over Sicily that day; its Mediterranean air entry for the night is a raid on Naples: 'One ship was sunk and four damaged in the course of an attack on Naples during the night of 9 Nov. ... Six of our planes were lost owing to strong night-fighter activity' (skl:51/p171, read on the page image). Naples is about 310 km from Palermo: a date match, not the cause of the alert. La Stampa of 10-11 Nov 1943 (the German communiqué) does not name Palermo (OCR searched). Battery D's report the same day: 'Usual field duties and instructions.' (rg64-456824820/p0853).

text: Battery went into yellow condition at 1605. 15 unidentified planes reported, returned to white condition at 1620 without sighting aircraft.
note: Battery C's own morning report (record of events after the 10 Feb form, p0670), read on the scan. No aircraft sighted. The only alert of January and February 1944 (rg64-461617355/p0686-p0748; rg64-463957373/p0651-p0711). The other side not found: the Naval Staff's diary for February 1944 (vol. 54) is not on the Internet Archive; La Stampa of 11-12 Feb 1944 does not name Palermo (OCR searched). Battery D's report the same day: 'Usual field duties and instructions.' (rg64-463957373/p0733).

text: Air Guard spotted HE 111 flying reconnaissance over area from about 1500 to about 1515. Radar picked it up. Out of range, no rounds fired.
note: Battery C, 62d AAA Gun Bn's own morning report (record of events typed with the 28 Mar entry, after the 28 Mar form, p0391), read on the scan. The aircraft type is the battery's identification. The only enemy aircraft in its reports from March and April 1944 (rg64-466426100/p0333-p0398; rg64-468998085/p0674-p0703). The other side: the German Naval Staff's diary for 27 Mar 1944, 'On 27 Mar. some planes executed reconnaissance flights in the central Mediterranean' (skl:55/p396), and under the German Naval Command Italy, 'Aerial photographic reconnaissance detected two cruisers thereof one lying in the dock, two destroyers, one escort vessel, one patrol boat, two LST's, eight LCT's, eight freighters, lying in the harbor of Palermo' (skl:55/p397; both read on the page images). The same day and the same harbour, so very likely the flight the battery saw; the diary gives no time or aircraft type, and does not name the unit. Battery D's report the same day: 'Usual field duties and instructions.' (rg64-466426100/p0457).

text: 8 ME 109's Btry fired 20 HE 230 rds .50 cal. 1530 (1) one plane damaged (1-21-44).
note: Record of events of 22 Jan, for 21 Jan. "20 HE" partly blotted on the scan. The battery at Lucenteforte; its detached sections were at Casale.

text: [3 EM] Wounded in Action (LW) and remaind on Dy 1600 (1-25-44).
note: On the 26 Jan form. Cause not typed. The record names the men.

text: 3 ME 109's strafed Btry fired 23 rds HE 475 rds of .50 Cal. No hits 1710.
note: Record of events, back of the 5 Feb form (p0755).

text: [a man] Dy & Det for rat 1st Bn 178th FA to Hosp LD Wounded in Action 1740; [a man] Wounded in Action (LW) and remaind on dy 1740.
note: Cause not typed. Corrected on 16 Feb (p0779): to "Abs Sk 401st Med Bn LD Wounded in action 1740. (LW in leg)". The record names the men. Half the battery's sections were then near St. Elia (p0798), so where the men were hit is not known.

text: [2 EM] Wounded in Action (LW) and remaind on dy.
note: No time or cause typed. The record names the men.

text: [a man] Fr dy to missing in action sn 1800 hrs Feb 11, 1944.
note: On the 14 Feb form; corrected 19 Feb (p0983): "EM missing instead of missing in action." The record names the man. 11 Feb was the day the 2nd Platoon had moved to Acquafondata (p0963).

text: In tactical position giving AA protection to FA. Gun Positions shelled by enemy art'y at 1500 hrs. Two casualties evacuated.
note: Record of events, back of the 21 Feb form. The form (p0987): two men to the 401st Coll Sta, 13th FA Brig, "SW in head and left arm by enemy shell fire 1500 hrs" and "SW in abdomen by enemy shell fire 1500 hrs" (the record names them). The German side: kit engagement venafro-1944-02.

text: 2 ME-109 mission unknown flying north over area, no hits. Time 1450A. 12 ME-109 bombing mission, 2 planes destroyed, 1500A. Heavy shelling all day.
note: Battery F at Selvone. The entry does not say who destroyed the two. Battery G at Filignano, about 2.5 km south, fired on the same raid at 1500A and claimed two destroyed (p0276): one raid seen from two batteries, so one claim, not two (inferred from the time and place).

text: Heavy shelling. Italian K.P. killed by enemy shell fire at position #25.
note: An Italian kitchen helper (K.P.), not a soldier of the battery. Battery F at Selvone.

text: 8 ME 109, mission unknown, positions engaged, no hits scored.
note: Battery F near Acquafondata. Batteries E (1530) and G (1535) fired on 8 Me 109s the same afternoon.

text: At 1225A fired at 2 ME 109's, 12rds 40mm & 80rds 50 cal expended. No hits claimed, withheld fire as 4 Spitfires appeared in range.
note: Battery G at Filignano, protecting the 938th FA.

text: At 1435A fired at 2 ME 109's, 91rds-40mm & 425 rds 50 cal expended. One destroyed.
note: Battery G at Filignano.

text: At 1500A fired at 12 FW 190's, dive bombing, 206 rds 40mm & 1035 - 50 cal expended. Two destroyed. One plane exploded and disintegrated in mid-air, the other lost wing and fell to earth.
note: Battery G at Filignano. Battery F at Selvone logged "12 ME-109 bombing mission, 2 planes destroyed, 1500A" (p0215): the same raid (inferred), the type differing between the two batteries.

text: At 1535A fired upon 8 ME 109s, flying at 2000 ft., expended 38 rds - 40mm and 40 rds - .50
note: Battery G at Viticuso. No hits.

text: At 1620A fired upon 2 ME109s, flying at 2000 ft, mission: reconnaissance, expended 182 rds ... One damaged.
note: Battery G at Viticuso; the rounds as the draft reads them: 182 of 40 mm and 1200 of .50.

text: At 1710 fired on 3 ME 109s, 123 rds - 40mm ... One damaged.
note: Battery G at Viticuso; 1,150 rounds of .50. Battery E at Lucenteforte fired on "3 ME 109's" at 1710 the same day (p0756): one flight seen by two batteries (inferred).

text: Engaged fire on hostile planes identified as 2 FW 190s' at 1315 hrs. Apparent objective: Reconnaisance. Ammo Expended: 46 90mm HE. E/A Claimed: None.
note: Battery A at Baraccone (not placed).

text: Opened fire on enemy A/C. Identified as FW 190s'. Apparent objective: Bridges. Ammo Expended: 14 rds 90mm HE. 1 E/A claimed as damaged.
note: Battery A at Baraccone.

text: Engaged fire upon hostile A/C identified as 2 FW 190's. Apparent objective: Reconaissance. Ammo Exp: 200 rds 50 cal ... E/A claimed as damaged or destroyed: None. Time: 0920A.
note: Battery A at Baraccone; the morning of the day Batteries F and G fired on the 1500 raid (engagement filignano-1944-01-12).

text: Vehicles and personnel strafed and shelled by enemy en route to St. Elia between 1300 and 1600 hrs on the road Aquafondata and St. Elia. Five EM hospitalized as a result of wounds received during the activity.
note: On the road from Acquafondata to St. Elia; five more with minor wounds stayed on duty (the draft). The record names the men.

text: Battery heavily shelled by enemy FA action between 1430 & 1500 hrs. Type of ammo used by enemy presumably 88's. Location of btry position believed to be revealed to the enemy as a result of (2) clip-winged Spitfires with proper British insignia ...
note: The battery did not fire on the two Spitfires; it suspected captured aircraft spotting for the Germans (its belief, not established).

text: Battery and immediate vic heavily shelled by German FA from 0900 to 0930. Approximately 30 shells burst in immediate area ... From 1400 to 1515, the battery again was subjected to heavy enemy FA action. Approx. 50 shells burst in immediate area. Action again believed to be result of direct ground observation. Damage: Heavy ...
note: Continued on p0630: a 90 mm gun installation "received direct hit causing piece to be temp. inactive"; "One EM killed in action, 2 EM wounded and hospitalized, 6 wounded remained duty"; a truck and trailer and the mess tent destroyed. The record names the men.

text: 8 P-40's Bombed & Strafed, 2d Platoon fired 39 rds of HE & 390 rds of .50 Cal. No hits (1830) (7-2-44)
note: Battery A, 894th AAA (the former Battery E, 67th CA (AA)) near Frosini, Tuscany. P-40s were Allied fighter-bombers; the entry doesn't say what they bombed and strafed or why the platoon fired. Same page: the 2nd Platoon moved to "Pieve. Scola RQ 61" to protect the 248th FA Bn, 12 miles.
